rationale: Lifecycle closes admission before awaiting shutdown and wakes an idle worker to drain all queued requests. Worker exit/fatal/init failure/pre-entry cancellation explicitly fails pending futures and balances queue accounting. Stop callers share the worker completion and cannot cancel it accidentally; repeated start is rejected, and completed restart recreates loop-bound queue/signals. Barrier and queue-full fixtures verify terminality, cancellation and sequential cross-loop reuse.

source_checks.observation: Rejects live double start; reset loop-bound primitives only after previous worker completion.
Closes admission synchronously and shields completion of the draining worker.
Drains accepted work; defers cancellation until the current SQL process settles and fails remaining queued futures.
Also settles the queue when cancellation happens before the worker first executes.

rationale: Encrypted retries compare authenticated canonical plaintext plus persisted event metadata, using the vault captured for the request. A matching retry returns the original seq/event_id/hash without rewriting ciphertext, timestamp or row. Missing/wrong original key and forced collision/metadata mismatch reject explicitly while later valid events still commit. Empty created_at retains the existing autogenerated-date semantics. UUID, SQL schema and historical chain hash format remain unchanged; this is row/result idempotency, not an exactly-once IPC guarantee.

rationale: Only _execute_insert_tx owns BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. It rolls back once only when a transaction is active; _process no longer rolls back a second time or closes the connection on ordinary rejection. ValueError/SQLite errors with confirmed clean state fail the current Future and allow subsequent work; failed rollback/uncertain state kills the writer and fails its backlog. SQL CHECK, commit-failure, rollback-failure and cancellation-during-commit fixtures independently observe rows, trace/transaction state and future outcomes.

source_checks.observation: Single transaction owner; failure cleans up only an active transaction and rejects unconfirmed rollback.
Recoverable request errors continue only with a clean connection; fatal failure settles backlog.
Delegates the transaction directly and acknowledges only the confirmed result, without a second rollback.

rationale: get_state_attestation obtains aggregates and leaves in separate SELECTs without an explicit read transaction, then verifies integrity through verify_chain's separate connection/snapshot. Concurrent appends can make total_entries/max_seq and the roots refer to different states. The isolated in-memory SQLite model confirms that this SELECT sequence can observe count 1 and two leaves after an intervening commit; the actual asynchronous ledger was not executed. anchor_to_rekor consumes the mixed fields without a snapshot/checkpoint comparison. Re-reviewed after Lot5: The attestation still combines a read context with a separate verification snapshot; its body is AST-identical and remains OPEN.

rationale: The client documents PEM public_key_pem and base64-encodes its UTF-8 bytes.
